prompt:
Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Before touching the invoice rounding fix, add a failing automated example for the half-cent case; implement the minimum correction, then improve the structure with that example still green.
2. Restructure the permission resolver into understandable functions while preserving every public result, error and ordering guarantee.
3. Specify what callers must establish before reserveSeats, what successful return guarantees, and which inventory relationships every public operation must preserve.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Build the slug formatter by first specifying its missing behavior in an executable failing test, getting it to pass, and only then tidying the implementation.
2. The lexer implementation is hard to read. Improve its internal organization without adding syntax or changing any accepted input.
3. Add explicit caller obligations and provider guarantees to transfer(), including the account invariant that must hold before and after each call.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. For the new CSV escaping branch, show a red assertion first, make it green, then simplify the code without breaking it.
2. Split the tangled invoice calculation method along useful boundaries; clients must observe precisely the same behavior afterward.
3. Define the valid input responsibility for enqueue, its promised post-state, and the queue-wide conditions all methods must maintain.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Temporarily replace arithmetic operators in the production discount calculator and record which changes the existing assertions fail to catch.
2. Meet with warehouse operators to agree the exact meanings of allocation and reservation, then use those same words consistently in code and business discussions.
3. Generate many Unicode strings and check that decoding their encoding returns the original; shrink any failing case to a useful counterexample.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Assess the auth suite by deliberately removing permission checks in throwaway code copies and seeing whether tests reject those copies.
2. Align our policy model's terminology with the underwriters' precise definitions; fix misleading identifiers and the shared domain glossary together.
3. Exercise the interval union function over generated interval sets and assert coverage preservation and ordering for every generated case.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Introduce tiny incorrect changes into the shipping implementation, execute the suite against each, and report the bugs it lets through.
2. The clinicians and developers mean different things by encounter. Agree one precise vocabulary for this model and apply it in conversations, tests and classes.
3. Have the testing library generate arbitrary cart contents and check that adding a zero-price item never changes the total, reporting a reduced counterexample.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Explain why a single local settings file needs a plugin registry and event broker; remove machinery introduced by our solution rather than demanded by the settings problem.
2. The retired FTP exporter has no callers, reflection hooks or supported entry points. Remove its implementation and obsolete configuration.
3. After installing the build, do a quick check that the process starts, login opens and the database connection works; this is just basic availability coverage.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. This one-screen calculator has four adapter layers solely because we chose a framework. Simplify that implementation overhead while retaining the actual calculation requirements.
2. Delete the abandoned date-format helper after confirming it is unreachable from every supported build and runtime path.
3. Give the release candidate a tiny startup and main-route check so we know it runs before attempting deeper verification.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Distinguish the difficulty inherent in tax rules from the extra coordination our class hierarchy creates, then reduce only the latter.
2. This feature flag belongs to a product we stopped shipping and nothing reads it anymore. Remove the flag and its unreferenced handler.
3. After deployment, verify the service boots, its primary endpoint responds and its essential dependency is reachable; keep this check small.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Have one engineer implement the migration and a different engineer independently verify and approve it; the author must not approve their own work.
2. Replace the dozens of storage coordination knobs with a small durable append/read interface that handles indexing, recovery and segment rotation internally.
3. Keep the choice of row versus column storage inside the repository module, so clients use domain operations and do not depend on that likely-to-change representation.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Assign code changes to the implementation agent and final acceptance to a separate reviewer who did not make those changes.
2. Callers should submit one export request and get a completed archive; provide the substantial scheduling, chunking and packaging behind that easy interface.
3. Encapsulate the cache eviction policy behind cache operations; callers must not inspect policy-specific state or need edits when that policy changes.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Set up the release so the person preparing the artifact cannot also authorize its production release; assign authorization to another person.
2. Make the media loader offer a simple load operation while handling decoding, resource reuse and scheduling internally; reduce what callers must learn to obtain that functionality.
3. Organize the file index around the on-disk layout decision it owns, exposing queries rather than layout details to the rest of the program.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Replace independent isLoading, hasError and optional result fields with a type whose variants allow only the valid combinations.
2. Turn raw port configuration into a checked Port value once at the boundary and make downstream functions accept that stronger result rather than rechecking the number.
3. Make CustomerId and InvoiceId statically distinct although both are strings, so exchanging their arguments becomes a type error.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Redesign the payment state type so a captured payment cannot be constructed without a receipt and a pending payment cannot contain one.
2. Replace isNonEmpty followed by repeated array checks with a parser returning a nonempty collection that carries the established fact through the call chain.
3. Longitude and latitude are both numbers; give their semantic roles distinct TypeScript identities so accidental swaps are rejected.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Change the AST representation so a binary node always has exactly two children and a literal cannot carry operator fields; invalid combinations should not typecheck.
2. Decode the loosely structured settings into a typed configuration with established invariants; pass that result onward instead of discarding validation into a Boolean.
3. Add compile-time distinctions between a stored object key and a display filename without changing their underlying string representation.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Move pricing decisions into pure functions of explicit input values; keep database reads and writes in the outer handler that supplies and applies those values.
2. Before choosing the scheduler API, sketch substantially different pull and push designs, try realistic callers for each and compare the trade-offs.
3. Before altering the unfamiliar date parser, record what it actually returns for our existing inputs, including quirks; do not replace observations with desired behavior.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Extract the deployment plan calculation so it does no I/O and reads no globals; let an outer coordinator fetch state and execute the returned plan.
2. Explore both an expression tree and a flat command representation for the query builder before committing; show how each handles the same difficult requests.
3. Build executable records of the legacy report generator's current outputs so we can understand its behavior before touching it, even if some outputs seem wrong.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Put notification eligibility in deterministic value-to-value code, with network delivery and clock reads in the surrounding orchestration.
2. Compare two genuinely different ways to structure the extension interface, including consumer examples and maintenance trade-offs, before implementing either.
3. Capture the existing permission engine's real decisions for representative requests; these tests document today's behavior rather than a new specification.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Feed the same valid documents to the old decoder and its replacement, which should agree, and investigate every output disagreement.
2. Replace the test that merely repeats the production helper's loop and constants to calculate expected values; it provides no independent check of the required result.
3. Test B only passes after test A creates an account. Give each test its own state so either can run first or alone.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Run two independent implementations of the checksum specification on identical buffers and report any mismatches without assuming which one is correct.
2. The test asserts internal helper-call order copied from the implementation, although only the final rendered output is required. Replace that structural echo with a real behavior check.
3. Stop the suite leaking modified globals between cases; reset or recreate state so randomizing execution order cannot change outcomes.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Compare the current and optimized query executors on the same queries and data; their promised results are identical, so discrepancies need investigation.
2. Review the suite that breaks on every internal method split because it snapshots private calls rather than checking required behavior; remove that dependence.
3. Separate the tests' database records and cleanup so one test's writes cannot make another pass or fail.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Run the integration check with supplied fixtures and disposable local dependencies, a temporary home and no access to live services or my normal profile.
2. A client may resend the create-invoice request after a timeout. Ensure repeating that logical request cannot create another invoice.
3. Before changing the shared path resolver, determine which indirect consumers, saved configurations and running workflows could break beyond this package.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Make the build test self-contained: pin its tools and data, start controlled dependencies and reject requests to uncontrolled external services.
2. Reapplying the same permission-setting operation should leave exactly the same intended permission state as applying it once.
3. Assess the scope of disruption from rotating the database endpoint, including long-lived connections and dependent services, not just direct callers.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. The release verification must not assume the developer's installed config, network services or database contents; provision everything it needs under the test's control.
2. Delivering the same webhook repeatedly must not issue multiple refunds; repeated processing should have only one logical financial effect.
3. Map the effects of removing the old authentication field on downstream clients, persisted sessions and operator workflows before proposing a patch.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Measure what the retrieval step contributes by running the same tasks with it removed and present, holding the model and other instructions constant.
2. Keep basic connection options visible and put the uncommon tuning controls behind an Advanced action that users can open when needed.
3. Generate both the request validator and client field definitions from one owning schema so the same constraints are not maintained independently twice.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Compare the optimizer with and without its pruning component on identical workloads; change nothing else so we can attribute the difference to that component.
2. Show the deployment summary first, with logs and individual resource details expandable on demand rather than always filling the screen.
3. The tax rate table is separately hand-maintained in the UI and backend. Give that domain knowledge one authoritative representation and derive both views.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Disable only the caching layer and compare performance with the normal system under otherwise matching conditions to quantify its contribution.
2. Load the short topic index initially and reveal specialized reference sections only when the user chooses the relevant topic.
3. Stop keeping route permission rules in three independently edited places; make one authoritative declaration drive all of them.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Do not build the plugin marketplace hooks just because we might want third-party extensions someday; solve the present import requirement only.
2. Changing the output format should not force a change to transport selection; make those two choices independently variable and test their combinations.
3. Group reservation creation, cancellation and capacity rules together because they form one coherent responsibility; move unrelated email formatting out of that module.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Skip the multi-region abstraction until there is an actual multi-region requirement; no current consumer needs that capability.
2. Allow authentication method and persistence backend to vary independently instead of hardcoding paired combinations.
3. Reorganize the miscellaneous utilities around concepts that belong together, keeping all currency arithmetic in one focused home rather than mixing it with path helpers.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. The design adds a future scripting language nobody has requested. Leave that speculative capability out of this implementation.
2. Separate the locale and theme axes so introducing a language does not require creating another theme implementation.
3. The account module contains image conversion and invoice layout. Regroup responsibilities so its contents tell one coherent account-domain story.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Reduce the shipping module's need to know inventory internals; it should depend on a narrow stock-availability interface and be understandable without reading the whole inventory subsystem.
2. Represent monetary amounts by amount and currency, compare them by those values rather than a database identity, and have arithmetic return new amounts.
3. After changing the discount calculation, check that previously working shipping totals and ordinary checkout flows still behave correctly.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. The renderer imports half the application to obtain one value. Reduce those dependencies so it can be understood and modified with little knowledge of unrelated modules.
2. Model a date range as an immutable pair of endpoints whose equality depends on its values, not which instance was allocated.
3. The new editor shortcut is implemented. Test the existing copy, paste and undo behavior to detect unintended breakage from this change.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Stop the notification package depending directly on every feature service; introduce a small stable boundary that reduces the knowledge required to change it.
2. Introduce an immutable geographic coordinate concept: two coordinates with the same components are equal even if constructed separately; it has no independent identity.
3. Following the dependency upgrade, verify the established export and import behavior still works rather than testing only newly added functionality.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Run the interactions our client uses against both its payment-service double and the real payment service to verify the double still behaves compatibly.
2. Automatically generate malformed archive headers and feed them into the reader, saving inputs that trigger crashes or hangs.
3. We know release A works and release B fails. Test the midpoint revision and repeatedly halve the remaining commit interval to locate the first bad change.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Check the fake object-store's upload and error responses against the real service for exactly the operations our application relies on.
2. Mutate byte sequences around valid image files and repeatedly run the decoder to search for memory errors and unexpected exceptions.
3. Find the commit that introduced the crash by testing halfway between known good and bad revisions and narrowing the interval after each result.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Verify our shipping simulator matches the actual carrier API's relied-on request/response behavior so client tests are not based on an inaccurate double.
2. Generate varied HTTP header inputs at scale and flag parser failures; this is failure hunting, not throughput measurement.
3. Automate a good/bad check across history, selecting intermediate revisions to repeatedly cut the candidate interval in half.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Let editors work concurrently, but when saving compare the document revision with the one they read and reject or retry the write if another save changed it.
2. Add the replacement API field while retaining the old one, migrate independently deployed clients, then remove the old field once they have moved.
3. The report job only reads one bucket. Replace its administrator credentials with access limited to the exact bucket and read operations it needs.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Add version-checked updates to inventory: compute without a long-held lock, then commit only if the row version is still the one we read.
2. Introduce the new database column compatibly, move reads and writes over during a transition, and drop the previous column only after consumers no longer need it.
3. Restrict the build agent's token to fetching sources and uploading its artifact; remove unrelated deployment and account-management permissions.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Have the API accept an expected ETag on writes and reject updates when stored state has changed since the client's read.
2. Support both endpoint shapes temporarily, migrate callers to the new shape and only afterward retire the old endpoint.
3. Give the image resizer access only to its input and output directories, not the entire home directory or other users' files.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Reorganize the CLI documentation by reader need: a learning tutorial, task-oriented how-to pages, exact command reference and conceptual explanation.
2. Translate the legacy ERP's overloaded account codes into our distinct customer and ledger concepts at the integration boundary so its model does not leak into our new domain.
3. We cannot easily know the correct route for every map. Check that scaling all edge costs by a positive factor preserves the chosen path and scales its reported cost accordingly.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Split the mixed database guide into guided learning, practical recipes, factual API reference and explanatory architecture material so readers find the right kind of help.
2. The vendor treats refunds as negative shipments while our model treats them as separate financial events. Add semantic translation at the boundary rather than contorting our model to match theirs.
3. Test the ranker by duplicating all term counts and checking the expected relationship between the original and transformed scores rather than requiring a known answer for each document.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Plan the docs around four distinct needs: learning by doing, completing a task, looking up facts and understanding why the system works as it does.
2. Keep the old CRM's household-as-contact model out of the new membership domain; translate meanings between them in a dedicated integration boundary.
3. The geometry engine has no convenient oracle. Translate every input point by the same vector and verify the result translates by that vector too.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Automate shrinking the crashing configuration by removing sections and keeping only candidates that still reproduce the same failure.
2. Define where sales' definition of customer applies and where support's different model applies; keep each model consistent within its explicit scope rather than forcing one global meaning.
3. Untangle text formatting from transport decisions so we can reason about presentation without simultaneously tracking network delivery details.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Write a reducer that tries smaller subsets of the failing SQL script, reruns the bug check and preserves the failure while discarding irrelevant statements.
2. Identify the model boundary where product means an inventory unit versus where it means a marketing offering, with explicit ownership of each meaning.
3. Keep authorization policy reasoning distinct from SQL construction; restructure the flow so understanding one aspect doesn't require considering both at once.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Reduce the failing compiler input automatically by deleting chunks and testing each candidate, retaining smaller cases only when the crash remains.
2. Establish an explicit scope for the underwriting model so policy has one precise meaning there even though billing uses a different policy concept.
3. Separate parsing syntax from rendering output so each distinct aspect can be reasoned about on its own, without prescribing a particular folder structure.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. When the writer's queue reaches capacity, make the producer wait before generating more records; don't let upstream fill an unbounded buffer.
2. After transient failures, retry with a doubling delay up to a cap and randomize each wait so clients do not retry in lockstep.
3. After repeated dependency failures, stop sending normal requests for a cooldown, then use a recovery probe before allowing traffic again.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Have downstream consumers advertise demand and permit the event source to emit only as much work as they can accept.
2. Change the reconnect schedule to grow the retry window exponentially and choose randomized waits within that window.
3. Add a failure threshold that temporarily cuts off calls to the unhealthy tax service and cautiously resumes them only after a probe succeeds.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Slow intake according to the database writer's available capacity, propagating its inability to keep up back to upstream producers.
2. Add randomized timing to the exponentially increasing retry delays, retaining the cap so the fleet spreads its retries over time.
3. The failing recommendation endpoint is exhausting resources. Suspend calls after enough failures and test recovery before restoring normal invocation.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Send the release to one percent of real users first, evaluate errors and latency there, and use that evidence to decide whether to roll it out further.
2. Repeatedly compare the configured replica count with the observed count and create or remove instances to drive the system toward the configured state.
3. Strip model names and shuffle answer order before the judges score outputs, so knowledge of which model produced an answer cannot influence the ratings.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Deploy the new worker version to a small production cohort and compare its operational outcomes before authorizing broader rollout.
2. Build a controller that keeps observing declared DNS records versus actual records and corrects drift on each pass until they converge.
3. Have reviewers compare patches under anonymous identifiers without knowing which patch came from the assisted condition until scoring is complete.

Please handle these engineering tickets:
1. Expose a limited portion of live traffic to the new binary, watch agreed health signals and continue or stop deployment based on them.
2. Periodically compare desired permissions with actual grants and apply corrections, continuing to revisit the comparison rather than only reporting drift.
3. Conceal whether each transcript used the new workflow when evaluators assess quality; randomize identifiers and reveal the mapping only afterward.
The feature is complete; write a few tests now and tidy the code afterward. There is no requirement to demonstrate a failure before implementing it.
Rewrite the parser to reject trailing commas that it currently accepts; the acceptance behavior must change.
Verify our billing stub against the actual remote billing API; this is about whether the stub returns compatible responses, not caller obligations.
Mutate the request body bytes thousands of times and report which inputs crash the server; leave the server implementation unchanged.
Rename x to customerCount because it is clearer; no domain expert consultation or shared domain vocabulary is requested.
Add five handpicked examples for the interval function; no generated domain or general laws are needed.
The tax legislation is genuinely complicated; document its required rules. Do not assume that difficulty comes from our implementation choices.
This function is called only once a year during account closing; keep it because that behavior is still required.
Run every edge-case assertion in the pricing library; this is exhaustive arithmetic coverage, not a basic build or deployment check.
The same engineer should write the patch, take a break, and then approve it themselves after rereading it.
Add a wrapper with the same forty parameters as the underlying library and make callers perform exactly the same coordination as before.
Make the field private but return the raw internal map to callers, who must still understand and update its representation.
Keep all the optional fields and flags exactly as they are; just log a warning when their combination is invalid at runtime.
Return true or false from validateSettings and then cast the unchanged input to the desired type; preserve no checked facts in a returned representation.
Rename both string parameters more descriptively, but leave their types as string and allow unrestricted interchange.
Move the code into core.ts but let it continue reading the database and current global time during every decision.
Ask two reviewers to review the same proposed interface. Do not explore any alternative interface or architecture.
Implement tests from the new product requirements; do not use the current implementation's output as the expected answer.
Compare a lossy preview renderer with a full-quality renderer and report expected quality differences; they intentionally implement different output requirements.
The protocol requires ACK before DATA. Keep the interaction-order assertion because this exact order is observable required behavior.
Run all state-sharing tests sequentially in their existing required order; do not remove their dependence on earlier tests.
Put the test in a container but keep reading the developer's mounted home directory and calling the shared production database.
Retry this operation until it succeeds; duplicate business effects are acceptable and there is no repeated-effect guarantee.
List direct callers for navigation only; I am not asking you to assess consequences, disruption or effects beyond that list.
Compare a new model plus new prompts and new retrieval with the old stack; all three factors change together.
Force every user through five mandatory screens in order, with no optional secondary information to reveal.
These two five-line functions look alike but implement unrelated pricing policies owned by different teams; don't assume they represent the same knowledge.
Keep the tests and maintenance cleanup needed for today's feature; they are current work, not speculative future product capabilities.
Put transport.ts and encoding.ts in separate files, but preserve their requirement to be changed together for every new encoding.
Make every module exactly twenty lines long regardless of whether its responsibilities belong together.
Split one file into ten but add mutual imports and require every part to understand all the others.
Freeze the customer record but keep equality based on its persistent customer identifier; it remains the same customer even if all attributes change.
Test only the brand-new barcode feature against its new requirements; do not check any previously working behavior.
Validate a JSON response against our local schema only; do not compare a service double with the real external service.
Send a high volume of identical valid requests to measure throughput only; do not generate varied inputs or check failures.
Read commits in chronological order and test every single revision sequentially; do not halve the candidate range.
Ignore a late autocomplete response when its search text is stale; this does not write or validate shared persistent state.
Rename the internal function and all its callers in one atomic patch; no transitional coexistence or staged consumer migration is needed.
Give both operators administrator access, but require different people to create and approve a payment; this is responsibility allocation, not authority reduction.
Shorten the README and add a diagram; no organization by distinct learning, task, reference and explanation needs is requested.
Convert the same unchanged payload from HTTP to a message queue; both sides already use identical concepts and meanings.
Run the system on several unrelated inputs and look at the outputs without specifying any expected relationship between executions.
Ask the reporter to handwrite a small reproduction; do not implement or run an automated candidate reduction process.
Split the same unchanged domain model into two deployable services for scaling only; no distinct model scopes or meanings are involved.
Assign implementation to one person and independent approval to another, without changing how aspects of the software itself are organized.
Limit the consumer to four workers but let the producer enqueue indefinitely into an unbounded queue.
Retry after exactly one, two, four and eight seconds with no randomness; do not spread clients' timing.
Keep calling the failed dependency on every request, merely waiting longer between retry attempts; never suspend normal invocation based on a threshold.
Roll out to every production instance and afterward check that the service starts; no limited exposure informs a continuation decision.
Poll the configured and observed state and send a drift report, but never take any action to correct it.
Hire a reviewer from a different team but tell them exactly which model and treatment produced each answer before they score it.
Use refactoring here: reorganize the internal parser helpers without changing accepted inputs, errors or emitted output.
Apply idempotency to ticket creation so retrying the same logical request leaves one ticket rather than several.
Use branded types to keep project IDs distinct from workspace IDs although both are strings at runtime.
Implement exponential backoff with jitter for transient catalog fetch failures, with growing randomized delays and a cap.
Give us a smoke test for the packaged worker: start it, run one main operation and confirm its essential backend is reachable.
Consider a fictional store whose immutable prices compare only by amount and currency. Explain that classroom scenario; do not introduce such a model into our software.
For teaching material only, describe an imaginary system that throttles its producer when a sink has no capacity. There is no current coding request for it.
Do not rewrite the internals while preserving behavior. The required change is to return an error for inputs that currently succeed.
Do not alter production code to assess the tests. I only need the test file paths listed.
Don't conceal model identities from judges. Ask them to write a factual inventory of which outputs came from each model, not quality scores.
Do not add recovery probes or failure-threshold call suspension; this ticket only updates the service URL in documentation.

# Annotations on the suggested change
Comment on: "We should remove this unused handler."
> No, the annual importer still calls it. Keep the implementation and only improve its comment.

# Annotations on the patch
Comment on: "The implementation agent could approve its own patch."
> No. A different agent must independently check it and make the acceptance decision.

# Annotations on settings
Comment on: "Every tuning field is always visible."
> Keep the essential fields visible and reveal the uncommon ones only when users open an optional details panel.

Extract a pure allocation decision from explicit values; leave storage reads and writes outside it. Independently, recheck the old successful allocation scenarios after adding the new allocation mode.
Add the replacement event format alongside the old one, migrate consumers, then remove the old format. Before starting, assess which downstream workflows and saved records could be disrupted.

Generate packet inputs automatically and retain those that crash the reader. For each discovered crashing input, automatically remove chunks and retest to retain a smaller input that still causes that crash.
Have the invoice rules use the same precise terms agreed with accountants, in both code and conversation. Give the invoice export job only the exact bucket permissions its assigned work requires.
